{
  "reviews": [
    {
      "benchmark": "arc",
      "instrument_review": "ARC-AGI-2 provides a clear test of producing exact answers to unfamiliar grid puzzles under specified conditions. Worked examples, separate development and evaluation sets, human difficulty checks and reviews for repeated rules support its construction. However, the human study covered a larger pool than the final test, and matching human difficulty does not establish equivalent difficulty for AI systems. Scoring is precise but needs careful explanation: each output grid receives credit only for an exact match within two attempts, while a problem can receive partial credit when only some of its inputs are solved. The resulting score describes success on these puzzles; it does not separately measure particular reasoning skills or establish broader intelligence. Verified evaluations record settings and spending limits, which helps comparisons, but their single-run policy and missing repeatability estimates leave small differences difficult to interpret. Public access, software tests and revision records support inspection, while exposure risks, incomplete score updates and differences between testing routes limit comparisons across reports.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "The benchmark tests inference from examples through exact completion of new coloured grids.",
        "Human solving results informed test selection and matching of the three sets for human difficulty.",
        "The inspected software averages within-problem fractions, so a score can include problems that were not fully solved.",
        "Public problems, scoring software, marking tests and dated corrections make substantial parts of the evaluation inspectable."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "Public corrections include changed squares and unclear examples, so the version used can affect results.",
        "Verified evaluations use one run, leaving reported scores without averaging over repeated runs.",
        "The change record does not recalculate every affected AI score, limiting comparisons across revisions.",
        "Public evaluation problems are exposed, and the hidden-data policy acknowledges that information could escape."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "Repeated identical-test results and uncertainty estimates are absent from the reviewed materials.",
        "No systematic study establishes sensitivity to instructions, grid presentation or software settings.",
        "The full marking system was not independently tested, and the complete archive of reported outputs and costs was not checked.",
        "No supplied study establishes prediction of language, social interaction or real-world work, or rules out every unintended route to high scores."
      ],
      "reinterpretations": [
        "Read a score as exact grid-completion performance under the reported version, settings, budget and exposure conditions.",
        "Do not interpret the average as the percentage of fully solved problems when problems contain multiple test inputs.",
        "Human difficulty matching supports the selection process but does not establish AI score stability or equivalent AI difficulty.",
        "Broader reasoning and intelligence claims remain unresolved by the supplied evidence; they are not disproved."
      ],
      "closing_note": "The main reporting ambiguity is the difference between software credit and the published meaning of a fully solved problem. Reports should specify that distinction, the test version and the evaluation route."
    },
    {
      "benchmark": "designqa",
      "instrument_review": "DesignQA offers a practical but narrow comparison of AI performance on finding and applying Formula SAE rules and interpreting vehicle materials. Real rules, designs and practitioner contributions support relevance to the stated tasks. They do not establish coverage of engineering documents generally. Its six groups provide useful distinctions between task types, but their sizes are very uneven and their marking methods differ. Equal weighting means the overall score expresses a particular balance between groups rather than the proportion of all questions answered correctly; the supplied evidence does not establish it as a measure of a single engineering ability. Wording-sensitive scoring and incomplete reference answers can also separate awarded credit from answer validity. Comparisons need particular care because systems receive different information supplies, small groups are sensitive to individual answers, and identical-condition repeatability is not established. Public materials permit useful inspection, but incomplete result records and unclear revision effects restrict reproduction. The strongest interpretation is performance on these specific tasks with the reported inputs and scoring rules.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "The questions cover six kinds of rule-finding, interpretation and design-checking tasks using real Formula SAE materials.",
        "Additional reviewers checked manually written questions, although coverage had stated exceptions.",
        "Reported experiments examine effects of supplied passages and visual features, showing that evaluation conditions matter.",
        "Public questions, instructions, scoring code and some responses support partial inspection of results."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "Question counts range from 1,192 for individual-rule retrieval to 16 for performance checking, yet the overall score weights all six groups equally.",
        "The paper documents credit affected by punctuation and valid related rules missing from reference answers.",
        "Systems receive either full rulebooks or retrieved passages, so comparisons include differences in information supply.",
        "All described scale-bar drawings comply with the rule, allowing an always-yes strategy to earn their decision credit.",
        "One released answer file has fewer rows than the paper's corresponding question count, and historical inputs, software and settings are not fully linked to every result."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "Reviewer disagreement rates, remaining answer errors and comprehensive marking accuracy and consistency are not established.",
        "Identical-condition repetition and sufficient uncertainty information for close rankings are missing; varying passages does not isolate repeatability.",
        "No human-engineer baseline or evidence of transfer to other technical documents or engineering projects is reported.",
        "A protected test set, systematic overlap checks and clear rules for training on questions or repeated submissions were not established.",
        "The inspected materials lacked a clear record of revision effects on scores, a licence file and complete reuse rules."
      ],
      "reinterpretations": [
        "Treat results as performance of an AI together with its supplied documents, retrieval process, instructions and visual inputs.",
        "Read the overall score as an equally weighted combination of heterogeneous groups, whose separate results also need inspection.",
        "Treat close rankings cautiously: one additional correct answer changes accuracy in the performance group by 6.25 percentage points.",
        "The always-yes opportunity demonstrates a scoring shortcut, not evidence that any tested AI used it.",
        "Missing reuse documentation does not establish that permission is unavailable or reuse is prohibited."
      ],
      "closing_note": "Unclear evaluation instructions concern training on released questions and repeated submissions. Reports also need clearer links between each result and its exact inputs, software version and scoring rules."
    }
  ]
}
